evidence.notes: Rufinus confirms Athanasius's role in consecrating Frumentius.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: A philosopher named Meropius of Tyre sailed to India with two boys Frumentius and Aedesius. The ship was seized and all killed except the boys who were brought to the king of Aksum. When the king died the queen asked Frumentius to help govern. Frumentius sought out Roman traders who were Christians and built churches. Later he traveled to Alexandria where Athanasius consecrated him bishop. He returned to Aksum and converted many including the king.
passage.notes: Primary Western source for the christianization of Aksum; Rufinus heard the account from Aedesius himself.
